newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche sees new drugs adding sales momentum.
newsitem.headline: Roche sees new drugs adding sales momentum.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said it expected the rapid global launch of three new products in the coming months and next year to give further momentum to sales from its pharmaceuticals division, the company's largest.
Roche is in the process of launching three new drugs, which the company and analysts' look to with great promise.
Posicor, against high blood pressure and angina pectoris has received approval in the U.S. and Europe. The other two drugs, Xenical and Tasmar, have not yet received final approval.
Xenical is new drug against obesity and Tasmar is against Parkinson's disease.

Roche also said in its half-year report that it expects sales to continue to grow "well ahead of the market average" in its diagnostics division due to strong demand for the new generation of fully-automated analysers and new PCR tests.

PCR, or polymerase chain reaction, is a technology that allows for tiny fragments of genetic material, DNA, to be copied millions of times in a brief period. It thus produces samples large enough for doctors to rapidly detect infectious diseases, cancer cells or inherited disorders.
The vitamins and fine chemicals division is expected to continue to improve its market position due to the development of cost-effective manufacturing process and new business segments.
The recent acquisition of Tastemaker and the improved global economic outlook will have a positive impact on the fragrances and flavours business, Roche added.
